cards.explanation: The answer is a wind, friends. That's all it takes. "And God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to subside." (Genesis 8:1) No big show, just a wind, and the water starts heading down.

The answer is False. The text says "The waters receded steadily from the earth, and after 150 days the waters had gone down." (Genesis 8:3) Steady is the word, friends. It was a long, slow process, and nobody could rush it.

The answer is the mountains of Ararat! "On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat." (Genesis 8:4) After all that floating, the ark finally stops moving. I bet Noah's family felt that settle under their feet. Me, I once spent years in a junk drawer, so I know what it's like to finally stop sliding around.

The answer is mountains! "…on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible." (Genesis 8:5) The waters kept receding until the tenth month, and now the tops of the mountains show. After years in the back of a junk drawer, I know how good it feels when something new finally comes into view. I bet Noah looked at that view for a good long while.

The answer is True. Noah sent out a raven, and "It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth." (Genesis 8:7) Back and forth, back and forth, that raven had a whole route going. I'm tired just picturing it, friends. I think that bird earned a long nap.

The answer is that she finds nowhere to land and returns. "…the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him in the ark…" (Genesis 8:9) The waters were still covering the surface of all the earth, so she had nowhere to land. Noah reached out his hand and brought her back inside the ark. I bet she was glad to see that hand.

The answer is an olive leaf, and a freshly plucked one. "…the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak." (Genesis 8:11) On her first trip she found no place to rest her foot (Genesis 8:9). This time she's carrying something, and I bet Noah noticed right away.

The answer is receded, friends. The text says, "So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth." (Genesis 8:11) That comes right after the dove shows up with the freshly plucked olive leaf. Noah didn't need a weather report, just a dove with good timing.
The answer is False. Genesis 8:12 says Noah "…sent out the dove again, but this time she did not return to him." Twice she came back to Noah. The third time, she stayed out there.

The answer is dry! "…Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry." (Genesis 8:13) The waters had dried up from the earth. I bet that was a sight after all that water. I'd have stared at that ground like it was a fresh batch coming out of the oven.

The answer is leave, friends. God says, "Come out of the ark, you and your wife, along with your sons and their wives." (Genesis 8:16) The earth is fully dry by then (Genesis 8:14). After all that time inside, I bet that was good to hear.

The answer is so they can spread out and multiply! God says the creatures should come out "…so that they can spread out over the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it." (Genesis 8:17) That means the birds, the livestock and everything that crawls. The animals have a whole earth waiting for them. That's a lot of creatures with a lot of room.

The answer is the clean ones! "…taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar." (Genesis 8:20) Noah builds an altar to the LORD, and the text says what he takes from: every kind of clean animal and clean bird. Clean is the word that counts here, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says in His heart, "Never again will I curse the ground because of man…" (Genesis 8:21) He says it right after Noah's offering, and He says it even though "…every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth." A promise like that is worth holding onto.

The answer is that it is evil from his youth. The LORD says, "…even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth." (Genesis 8:21) It's a heavy line, friends, and I think it's worth slowing down on. He says it right alongside "Never again will I curse the ground because of man…"

The answer is False. What the LORD says in His heart is, "And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done." (Genesis 8:21) That's the opposite of someday doing it again. He says it once more when He makes His covenant: "never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth." (Genesis 9:11)

The answer is True. God says, "But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it." (Genesis 9:4) Right before that, He says, "Everything that lives and moves will be food for you…" (Genesis 9:3). So it's a big yes with one rule attached, friends. The catch is the lifeblood.

The answer is that God made mankind in His own image. God says, "for in His own image God has made mankind." (Genesis 9:6) That's the reason given for treating human life so seriously. The reason is who made people and whose image they carry.

The answer is False. God says He establishes His covenant "…with every living creature that was with you…" (Genesis 9:10) That's the birds, the livestock and every beast of the earth. Noah's family and the animals are all in it, friends.

The answer is the waters of a flood. God says, "Never again will all life be cut off by the waters of a flood…" (Genesis 9:11) That's the promise of the covenant. He adds, "never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth." Waters were the whole story here, so waters are the promise.

The answer is His rainbow! God says, "I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth." (Genesis 9:13) He calls it His rainbow, and He sets it in the clouds. Next time you spot one, friends, you'll know what it's a sign of.

The answer is that He will remember His covenant. God says, "I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of every kind." (Genesis 9:15) Then in the next verse He adds, "…I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant…" (Genesis 9:16). That's a promise with a sign hung up in the sky, and I like a promise I can look up and see. Whenever clouds form and that rainbow shows, you know what it's about.

The answer is everlasting, friends. God says, "…I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of every kind that is on the earth." (Genesis 9:16) Earlier He called it "…a covenant for all generations to come…" (Genesis 9:12). That word doesn't have an expiration date.
